plan.planning_summary: This study addresses a dual-stopband narrowband bandpass filter for 1550 nm LiDAR reception. The core challenge is achieving ≥0.95 transmittance at 1550 nm while suppressing both 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands within 30 layers using Ta2O5/SiO2. Three genuinely distinct strategy axes are proposed: (1) symmetric Fabry-Perot cavity with quarter-wave Bragg mirrors testing whether classical periodic stacks can achieve dual stopbands, (2) asymmetric cavity positioning testing whether breaking symmetry improves one stopband at the expense of the other, and (3) non-periodic thickness distribution testing whether aperiodic designs outperform periodic quarter-wave stacks for this specific dual-rejection requirement. Literature L06 directly motivates the dual-stopband approach, L09 informs the quarter-wave stack design principle, and L19 supports exploring non-periodic alternatives. Routes differ in topology structure and what thickness variables are optimized, ensuring each axis explores independent design space.

routes.scientific_hypothesis: A symmetric Fabry-Perot cavity structure with quarter-wave Bragg mirrors on both sides can achieve ≥0.95 transmittance at 1550 nm while providing adequate suppression in both 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm stopbands within 30 layers.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness (QWOT) alternating high/low index layers create high-reflectance Bragg mirrors. A half-wave cavity layer between two identical mirror stacks produces a narrow transmission peak at the design wavelength. Symmetry ensures balanced stopband performance on both sides of the passband.
